headline: Russell comes out on top after 4 lead changes in Melbourne
standfirst: George Russell won the Australian Grand Prix for Mercedes, finishing 2.974s ahead of Kimi Antonelli, with Charles Leclerc completing the podium after 58 laps of Melbourne.

sections.title: The start
sections.body: George Russell lined up first on the grid. Leclerc got the better launch and led the field across the line at the end of the opening lap. The biggest winner of the opening lap was Sainz, up 7 places to 14th.

sections.title: How it unfolded
sections.body: The lead changed hands 4 times. Laps led: Russell (32), Leclerc (23) and Hamilton (3). Russell took the lead for good on lap 28. The race ran green from start to finish.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Russell made 1 stop, running medium → hard tyres. The field made 26 pit stops in total; the quickest stationary time was 2.2s for Leclerc on lap 18. 10 of the top 10 finishers got home with one stop or fewer.

sections.title: Movers
sections.body: Max Verstappen made up the most ground, climbing 14 places from 20th to 6th. Lawson went the other way, slipping from 8th to 13th. Timing recorded 299 on-track position changes, 24 of them by Sainz.

sections.title: Retirements
sections.body: Hadjar (lap 11), Alonso (lap 22) and Bottas (lap 16) failed to finish. Hulkenberg and Piastri did not take the start.

sections.title: Conditions and pace
sections.body: It stayed dry throughout. Track temperature ranged from 34°C to 39°C, with air at 24–25°C. Max Verstappen set the fastest lap, a 1:22.091 on lap 43.
